name: Terminal Manager
description: Local terminal session registry and TUI detector. Tools are available to all scripts via AskMac MCP — not exposed to iPhone.

tools.name: register_session
tools.description: Register a terminal session for monitoring. Called by app scripts when a session starts.

tools.name: unregister_session
tools.description: Remove a session from the registry.

tools.name: detect_tui
tools.description: Run hook patterns against recent session output. Returns first match or null.

tools.name: read_output
tools.description: Return recent output lines from a session.

tools.name: send_key
tools.description: Send a named key to a session.

tools.name: send_text
tools.description: Clear the current input line, type text, press Enter.

tools.name: send_raw
tools.description: Write a raw string to the session without modification.

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: Return all registered sessions.

tools.name: inject_tty
tools.description: Inject text into the TTY input queue via TIOCSTI — no clipboard, no Terminal.app focus required. Falls back to tmux send-keys for tmux sessions.

tools.name: focus_window
tools.description: Bring the terminal window or tmux pane for this session to the foreground without typing anything.

tools.name: wait_for_idle
tools.description: Poll the session until the Claude Code idle prompt appears, then return the response text above it. Works for both TTY and tmux sessions.

tools.name: create_window
tools.description: Create a named tmux window in a session. Ensures the session exists first. Optionally runs a command inside the new window and sets its working directory. Returns the target string (session:window_name) you can pass to other tools.

tools.name: destroy_window
tools.description: Kill a tmux window by target string. Sends Ctrl+C first unless force=true, then runs kill-window. Also unregisters any registered session whose tmux_target matches.

tools.name: list_windows
tools.description: List all windows in a tmux session. Returns index, name, target, active flag, current command, and whether the pane is alive. Returns an empty list if the session doesn't exist.

tools.name: rename_window
tools.description: Rename a tmux window. Pass the current target (session:name or session:index) and the new name. Raises an error if the window doesn't exist.

tools.name: split_pane
tools.description: Split a tmux pane into two. direction='horizontal' places the new pane side-by-side; direction='vertical' stacks it above/below. Optionally runs a command in the new pane. Returns both the original target and the new pane's target string.

tools.name: pane_alive
tools.description: Check whether a tmux pane is still running. Returns alive=true/false. Use this to poll after launching a command to know when it exits.

tools.name: get_pane_info
tools.description: Return full metadata for a tmux pane: pid, current command, alive state, width, height, tty, window name, and session name.

tools.name: send_interrupt
tools.description: Send Ctrl+C to a tmux pane to interrupt the running process. Accepts either a direct tmux target string or a registered session_id (at least one is required).

tools.name: wait_for_pattern
tools.description: Poll a tmux pane until a regex pattern matches in the recent output, then return the output. Use stable_count to require multiple consecutive matching reads before returning. Accepts target or session_id.

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Run a shell command in an ephemeral tmux window, wait for it to finish (shell prompt or pane exit), then return the full output. Set keep_window=true to leave the window open after the command completes.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Capture the current state of a tmux pane as text (always) and optionally as a base64-encoded PNG image of the terminal window (format='image' or 'auto'). Accepts target or session_id.

tools.name: migrate_to_tmux
tools.description: Migrate a running terminal session (TTY) into a tmux-owned window. Detects the shell's cwd automatically, creates a named tmux window there, and updates the session record so all subsequent tool calls use tmux. Optionally runs a command in the new window (e.g. 'claude' to resume a Claude Code session). Pass session_id for a registered session, or tty directly for an unregistered one.
